evidence: Only 2 packages (bin, test) with shallow directory depth (max 2), indicating minimal modular structure
Single main entry point file bin/q.py (~1200 lines) with monolithic control flow and direct CLI handling
High average fan-out (7.67) across modules suggests tight coupling rather than decoupled layers
Direct imports of sqlite3, csv, argparse, six, io, etc. without adapter/abstraction layers
Test suite in test/test_suite.py imports directly from bin.q, indicating procedural dependency
No clear separation of concerns (e.g., no separate controller/model/view or adapter layers)
Core logic resides in QTextAsData class with execute() method that orchestrates input parsing, SQL execution, and output in a single flow
MaterializedState hierarchy uses inheritance but remains tightly coupled to SQLite operations and file I/O
Exception classes defined at module level alongside core logic, not grouped in dedicated layers
risks: Difficulty scaling due to monolithic command-line tool nature
Hard to test core logic in isolation due to high fan-out and direct I/O
Low reusability of data processing logic outside CLI context
Potential maintenance challenges as codebase grows linearly without architectural boundaries
